title: Parsing error focuses script using incorrect class instead of incorrect class script itself
body: ### Godot version    v4.0.beta.custom_build [767f8fb48]    ### System information    Linux Ubuntu 20.04 with Unity desktop    ### Issue description    This seems to be a regression from Godot 3.    Previously, when a script had a parsing error, and some other scripts were referencing that script class, when trying to start the game, the code editor would focus on the script actually containing the error. (Note: I'm not sure about this, as Godot 3 didn't use generational ID; maybe the parsing order was undetermined)    It is now focusing on some unrelated script that just happens to reference the class of the incorrect script. While it is logical that there is a chain reaction preventing the processing of further scripts, in terms of UX, it is much more useful for the developer to focus the first incorrect line on the script that is actually incorrect.    ### Steps to reproduce    Note: the attached project replaces steps 1-3    1. Add a script Correct.gd  2. THEN, add a script Incorrect.gd (the order matters as the script parsing seems to follow the new generational id in Godot 4). Use `class_name Incorrect` so it can be referenced. Add some bad code, e.g. `func _ready(incorrect): pass`  3. Go back to Correct.gd and add some line reference Incorrect (e.g. declaring a variable of type Incorrect).  4. Try to play the game    Expected: the parsing error is focused on Incorrect.gd  Actual: the usage of the Incorrect in Correct.gd is focused    ### Minimal reproduction project    [Minimal repro - v4.0.beta.custom_build [767f8fb48] - Class usage is focused instead of parsing error.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9997981/Minimal.repro.-.v4.0.beta.custom_build.767f8fb48.-.Class.usage.is.focused.instead.of.parsing.error.zip)

title: Hovering over large variable in debugger shows wrong value at best, causes GPU issues at worst
body: ### Godot version  Master https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/03694757735d2331b157478f2337b3a87421ac92  ### System information  Win10 Gt 1030, (both GL and Vulkan)  ### Issue description  When hovering over a large variable in the debugger for example an array with 10_000_000 elements the value shown will be `<null>` instead of the actual array content. the thing is: checking if the array is actually null by doing `print(array == null)` shows that it is not null. title: Text Shader Previewer crashes inside loops
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproductible in 4.7.dev [34777ad] and after  ### System information  Windows 11 - Forward +  ### Issue description  Adding preview breakpoints to a text shader can lead to crashes. For example:  If you have a loop that does something like: ``` 1 - float x = 0.0; 2 - while(x < 0.5) { 3 -  float temp = x + 0.1; 4 -  x += 0.1 5 - } ```  Placing a breakpoint on line 4 is okay, but placing a breakpoint on line 3 creates an infinite loop because the line `x += 0.1` gets removed.  ### Steps to reproduce  - Create a shader containing a while loop. For example: ``` ... void fragment() {   ...   float x = 0.0;   while (x < 0.5) {     float temp = x + 0.1;     x += 0.1;   } } ... ```  - Place a breakpoint on line 4 - see that it is okay - Place a breakpoint on line 3 - see that it creates an infinite loop because the line `x += 0.1` gets removed.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  [mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26783781/mrp.zip)

title: Dragging and dropping files from 7zip into a Godot project fails.
body: ### Tested versions    5d62e12fcbd46034dd06f91c2b20bdd366f3a0c9    ### System information    Windows 11    ### Issue description    Windows and third-party software specific issue:  Dragging and dropping files from an archive with 7zip currently does not work. It appears that 7zip will create a copy of the files being dragged from the archive in the Windows temp folder, and delete it once the action has finished. It seems the APIs being used to give drag and drop awareness on Windows are only responsive after 7zip deletes this temp file, resulting in an error. title: The viewport pixel grid is misaligned and innacurate in Godot 4 beta 9
body: ### Godot version  4.0-beta9 (Standard and .NET6)   ### System information  Windows 11 22H2, RTX 3080 (527.37)  ### Issue description  In Godot 4, the pixel grid is slightly misaligned from the true position of pixels. Objects placed near the world origin will appear to fit within the pixel grid, but the grid will become steadily more misaligned the farther an object is from world origin. This causes critical visual issues in lower resolution projects, breaks tilemaps, and makes it impossible to make "pixel perfect" games in Godot 4.    Here is an example I was provided by another user, who used a 1px x 1px TextureRect that has been placed at two varying positions in the scene.  ![example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/121070110/208594359-4406b3ea-f222-420d-b06a-02900b52222e.png)    Here is a comparison between how sprites appear in the editor vs. how they appear in-game, which displays the massive side effects that this bug has on visual quality of certain games:  ![example2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/121070110/208597250-39345ec4-ef56-43c5-98c5-d0538cfc4418.png)  ### Steps to reproduce  - Start a new project in Godot beta 9  - Create a 2D scene and add a ColorRect that's 1 px by 1 px in size  - Go to "Viewport Snapping Options", turn on Pixel Snap, and then click "Configure Snap"  - Change the "Grid Step" option to something like 1x1, 2x2, etc. and press OK.  - Drag the 1x1 ColorRect from the world origin. The farther it is, the more misaligned.  ### Minimal reproduction project  No reproduction project necessary (UI bug)

title: Error "Unreferenced static string to 0: interface_added" on editor startup
body: ### Godot version  9580769e9a8e9542e651859d61452a13cf1eb398  ### System information  Archlinux 6.0.6-arch1-1 kernal, X11  ### Issue description  Hello  When starting the editor on the latest dev build I get these errors  ```  ERROR: BUG: Unreferenced static string to 0: interface_added     at: unref (core/string/string_name.cpp:131)  ERROR: BUG: Unreferenced static string to 0: interface_added     at: unref (core/string/string_name.cpp:131)  ```    I spent some time investigating this and I think this happens when the app tries to select the best GPU to use for rendering. Here is where I think the issue is:  In the `detect_prime()` in the `detect_prime_x11.cpp` file. There is a call to `fork()` on line 152.  As far as I understand, this call is supposed to make the sub processes try and make an X11 session then relay the best selected gpu back to the main process. I think the issue comes when these processes finish and `exit()` gets called. They try to free global memory(call global destructors) and thats where they run into this error and output it to console.    The reason I suspect this is because I ran the editor with gdb with `-gdb-set follow-fork-mode child` and the error only happens on the call to `exit()` on line 211 in `detect_prime_x11.cpp` in the sub process.    Removing the call to `emit_signal()` in `text_server.cpp` causes the error to not show up. I suspect that doing this causes the static string to not be allocated and thus does not show in the sub processes so no error because there is no call static object destructors.    I don't know why freeing the static object causes this error. If anyone could have a look at this to confirm that I am on the right track or if this is completely unrelated.  Thanks   ### Steps to reproduce  Start the editor on the latest commit with a dev build and observe terminal output.  ### Minimal reproduction project  _No response_

body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in v4.6.2.stable, v4.6.3.stable   ### System information  Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900HX (32 threads) - 47.72 GiB memory  ### Issue description  In our project we always get an unknown low lever error spam from the engine: ``` E 0:00:01:420   instance_set_scenario: BUG, indexing did not unpair geometries from light.   <C++ Source>  servers/rendering/renderer_scene_cull.cpp:835 @ instance_set_scenario() E 0:00:01:420   instance_set_base: BUG, indexing did not unpair geometries from light.   <C++ Source>  servers/rendering/renderer_scene_cull.cpp:607 @ instance_set_base() ```  The error does not report which objects are causing the issue; it is a low level sanity check unintelligeble by the end user. Over the course of a session this gets reported hundreds+ times and we have no information on what to change to fix it. As of now I am unaware of any actual sideffects outside of the error log.     ### Steps to reproduce  After deeper investigations i was able to narrow down the repro steps to the following: - Have a mesh close to a light with a layer matching the cull mask of the light, - Now change the layer of the mesh with by using `.layers` or `.set_layer_mask()` repeatedly over some frames - delete the light - upon deletion the engine throws the low level error about the failed unpairing (without any context)  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  [godot-light-pairing-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30603107/godot-light-pairing-mrp.zip)  Got an even shorter MRP: ``` extends Node3D ## Minimal repro for the "BUG, indexing did not unpair geometries from light" engine error.  func _ready() -> void: 	var light = OmniLight3D.new() 	light.omni_range = 10.0 	light.light_cull_mask = 1  	light.position = Vector3.ZERO 	add_child(light)  	var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new() 	mesh_instance.mesh = BoxMesh.new() 	mesh_instance.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_ON 	mesh_instance.position = Vector3(0, 0, -1) # inside the light's range 	mesh_instance.layers = 1 # starts matching the light's cull mask so it gets paired 	add_child(mesh_instance)  	print("REPRO: setup done, light_cull_mask=%d mesh.layers=%d" % [light.light_cull_mask, mesh_instance.layers]) 	for x in 5: 		await get_tree().process_frame 	mesh_instance.layers = 2 	print("REPRO: changed mesh layer") 	for x in 5: 		await get_tree().process_frame 	print("REPRO: freeing light instance now (mesh.layers=%d)" % mesh_instance.layers) 	light.queue_free() 	for x in 5: 		await get_tree().process_frame 	get_tree().quit()  ```

title: Integer overflow in RenderingDevice::_texture_create_reinterpret_buffer() buffer size calculation
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: 4.7.dev  ### Issue description  In `servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:2567-2568`, the buffer size calculation for texture reinterpretation has two bugs:  ```cpp uint32_t pixel_bytes = get_image_format_pixel_size(p_texture->format); uint32_t row_pitch = STEPIFY(p_texture->width * pixel_bytes, row_pitch_step); uint64_t buffer_size = STEPIFY(pixel_bytes * row_pitch * p_texture->height * p_texture->depth, transfer_alignment); ```  **Bug 1: Integer overflow.** `pixel_bytes * row_pitch` is `uint32_t * uint32_t` arithmetic that overflows before being implicitly converted to `uint64_t`. For a 16384x16384 RGBA8 texture: `pixel_bytes=4`, `row_pitch=65536`, `pixel_bytes * row_pitch = 262144`, `262144 * 16384 = 4,294,967,296` — overflows `uint32_t`, wraps to 0.  **Bug 2: Double-counting pixel_bytes.** `row_pitch` already equals `width * pixel_bytes`, so the formula should be `row_pitch * height * depth`, not `pixel_bytes * row_pitch * height * depth`.  This produces a zero-size or incorrectly-sized GPU buffer, causing out-of-bounds writes when texture data is uploaded.  ### Steps to reproduce  1. Create a large texture (e.g., 16384x16384 RGBA8) that requires a shared fallback buffer. 2. The buffer is allocated with incorrect size, leading to GPU memory corruption.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  N/A — arithmetic bug visible from source analysis.

title: PopupMenu doesn't inherit Texture Filter from project or parents
body: ### Tested versions  Reproducible in: 4.5.1.stable (Steam) Untested in any further version  ### System information  Godot v4.5.1.stable (f62fdbde1) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8129) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600KF (20 threads) - 63.81 GiB memory  ### Issue description  PopupMenu (as a child of OptionButton) doesn't inherit the Default Texture Filter from both its parent and the project itself. title: Theme.get_type_list() does not list empty type variations
body: ### Godot version    v4.1.2.stable.arch_linux    ### System information    Godot v4.1.2.stable unknown - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 23 Sep 2023 16:57:15 +0000 - Tty - Vulkan (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) HD Graphics 4600 (HSW GT2) () - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-4590 CPU @ 3.30GHz (4 Threads)    ### Issue description    Theme.get_type_list() does not list theme type variations for which no theme item (no constant, no icon, no font, etc) has been set.    Not only is it inconsistent with the behavior description in the docs, and with how Themes are saved as resources (because you can save empty theme variations by calling Theme.set_type_variation("Foo", "Control")), it is inconsistent with Theme.get_type_variation_list(), which does list all type variations regardless of whether theme items have been set for them or not.    This bug means it's impossible to retrieve a full list of type variations (since as far as I can tell, there's no way to list all base_types for which a type variation exists, for example). In essence, the theme resource is partially write-only.    The reason for this bug is quite simple: the code for get_type_list() goes through all the different theme items (fonts, icons, styles) and gathers all theme types, whereas get_type_variation_list() goes through all the variations of the given base_type, regardless of theme items.    The fix is quite simple: inside get_type_list(), for every base_type in variation_base_map, add to the HashSet every type variation associated with that base_type, mimicking get_type_variation_list().    Code links:  get_type_list(): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3f045951edb9229759644205e155e0a62490ef7a/scene/resources/theme.cpp#L1205  get_type_variation_list(): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3f045951edb9229759644205e155e0a62490ef7a/scene/resources/theme.cpp#L1153    ### Steps to reproduce    ```GDScript  var theme := Theme.new()    theme.set_type_variation("Foo", "BoxContainer")  print(theme.get_type_list().has("Foo")) # should print true, but prints false  print(theme.get_type_variation_list("BoxContainer")) # prints true, as is logical    theme.set_theme_item(Theme.DATA_TYPE_CONSTANT, "separation", "Foo", 42)  print(theme.get_type_list().has("Foo")) # now it prints true  print(theme.get_type_variation_list("BoxContainer")) # still prints true  ```    ### Minimal reproduction project    N/A

title: OptionButton popup stops responding after first tap on iOS Safari
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: 4.7.dev (master, commit 4bd85ce4b0 and later — after merge of #110893) - Not reproducible in: 4.7.dev with #110893 reverted (tested by reverting merge commit 4bd85ce4b0 locally) - Regression introduced by: #110893 (BaseButton: multitouch support) - Reproducible: iPhone (iOS Safari) - Not reproducible: Android Chrome, desktop Chrome  ### System information  Godot v4.7.dev (1aabcb9e9) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9602) - AMD Ryzen 9 9900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 61.66 GiB memory  ### Issue description  After #110893 changed BaseButton to consume screen (touch) events directly when a touchscreen is available, OptionButton's PopupMenu becomes unresponsive on mobile browsers after the first tap.  On a touchscreen device: - First tap on OptionButton shows the popup correctly. - After the popup is dismissed (by selecting an item or tapping outside), subsequent taps on any OptionButton in the scene no longer open the popup. - A brief highlight flash is visible on release, suggesting the press state is being processed but show_popup() is either not called or is immediately cancelled.  This does not happen on desktop browsers (mouse input path). Reverting the merge commit of #110893 restores correct behavior.  Workarounds tried that did not help: - input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch=false - input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse=false   ### Steps to reproduce  1. Open the MRP and export for Web. 2. Host the build and open it on a mobile browser (physical device; DevTools touch emulation may not reproduce). 3. Tap the OptionButton → popup appears, select any item (or tap outside to dismiss). 4. Tap the OptionButton again → popup does not appear.   ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  [mrp-110893.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26678548/mrp-110893.zip)  [mrp-110893-export.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26678581/mrp-110893-export.zip)

title: "Invalid break insert count" error when using a ligature font and a symbol that requires a hyphen.

title: StyleBoxFlat downscaling corner radius causes incorrect rendering with border width and anti-aliasing set
body: ### Godot version  4.0.beta4  ### System information  macOS 12.6.1  ### Issue description  A StyleBoxFlat (and possibly other StyleBox types) with corner radius set will downscale the corner radius if they are too large to fit. For example setting a 20px radius on all corners and scaling the box to be just 30px wide will result in 15px radius corners. This is useful since you can then basically make Styleboxes that are round or have rounded ends at any size < 2*the corner radius.     The issue is that as you can see this downscaling doesn't work correctly if you have a border width set for the StyleBox. It seems this messes up the downscaling size calculation somehow, so the middle vertices become misaligned, resulting in graphical artifacts. Especially if you have alpha blending on the BG Color:    https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17763524/201317258-5d6274e6-8095-4359-97f0-2822f3c34756.mov        ### Steps to reproduce  Setup:  - Create a Panel in a new 2d scene  - Set the panel to use a new StyleBoxFlat ThemeOverride style  - Set the BG Color to be a semi-transparent color  - Set a border width on all sides (larger like 5 for more obvious result)  - Set a corner radius on all corners (larger like 20 for more obvious result)    - Now, resize the Panel and observe an overlap appear in the middle as described above if the panel is made smaller than 2xCorner radius so downscaling of the radius is applied.  ### Minimal reproduction project  See steps to reproduce, should work in any project?

title: Unexpected crash when updating gui_embed_subwindows to false with extra windows active
body: ### Tested versions    Reproducible in 4.1.3, 4.2 stable    ### System information    Godot v4.2.stable - Windows 10.0.22621 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.3699) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700F CPU @ 2.90GHz (16 Threads)    ### Issue description    NB: Tested on the root viewport.    gui_embed_subwindows being updated during runtime with windows active causes strange results.     I see that this makes sense if you take it as given that this value represents that the root viewport should or should not have external windows, and we have some and are setting it to not be able to have any, so presumably there are some underlying functions that won't interact with the external windows as expected in this state. (And vice versa for embedded)    On the off chance someone else is having trouble with this: I have been able to workaround the issues by ensuring that any external windows are freed prior to updating the value when external windows are present. I assume alternatively you could reparent them to another viewport in the interim if your use case for some reason requires they be retained.     ```func _process(_delta):  	if Input.is_action_just_pressed("debug"):  		if get_child_count() > 0:  			get_child(0).queue_free()  			await get_tree().process_frame  		get_tree().root.get_viewport().gui_embed_subwindows = !get_tree().root.get_viewport().gui_embed_subwindows  	elif Input.is_action_just_pressed("debug_2"):  		if get_child_count() > 0:  			get_child(0).queue_free()  		var new_window = window_scene.instantiate()  		add_child(new_window)  ```  Alternatively I feel that having multiple viewports and not relying on changing the gui_embed_subwindows value to manage external Vs. embedded windows in your game is probably the **sanest** approach.   ### Steps to reproduce    See MRP    "1" - Spawns a window, freeing the previous  "2" - Change the gui_embed_subwindows value  "3" - Try to hide the first window in the list    Pressing 1, 2, and then 3 results in a crash as we start by spawning an external window, changing gui_embed_subwindows to true, then attempt to interact with the external window by hiding hiding it    Pressing 1, 2, and then 1 results in an orphaned window which godot doesn't have in the remote tree  This changes visually to being entirely full of black once it is refreshed by e.g. resizing it.    Starting by pressing 2 once and then any combination of 1 and 3 will seemingly not result in the same issues, nor will you run into an issue after pressing 2 again regardless of the embedded window state e.g. 2 - 1 - 2 - 1 or 2 - 1 - 3 - 1.     Edit: With 2 - 1 - 2 - 3 - 3 - 3 we end up with our previously embedded window as an external window, while still retaining the embedded window. When toggling its visibility it switches between a broken embedded window and hidden external window, and a working embedded window with a working external window. title: class_name doc comments before class are overridden by doc comments after it
body: ### Tested versions  Reproducible in v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]  Class doc comments were added in d1231be1c8f8f2c16fd1047adcd3c7f997a07c1f, but I haven't checked if it occurred in that build.  ### System information  Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6590) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 Threads)  ### Issue description  If you put it before class_name but have other `##` comments followed by a blank line, they override the class doc comment.  It seems like the first `##` in a file should be the doc comment and other should either be appended to it or ignored. Using the last one seems less likely to be correct.  ## Workaround  Make sure any following doc strings are attached to another line (no blank whitespace): ```gdscript ## Force the global rotation to stay at 0 (never rotate). class_name NilRotation extends Node2D   ## Run every frame. func _process(_dt):     global_rotation = 0 ```  ### Steps to reproduce  Put doc comment before (or after!) class_name but have other `##` comments, they override the doc comment: ```gdscript ## Force the global rotation to stay at 0 (never rotate). class_name NilRotation extends Node2D   ## Run every frame. (Oops, this becomes the class doc string.)  func _process(_dt):     global_rotation = 0 ```  ![completely wrong comment](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/568e7a6a-7806-4812-8c96-75d356e655df)  Or write a doc comment that contains a blank line for space:  ```gdscript class_name NilRotation extends Node2D ## Force the global rotation to stay at 0 (never rotate).  ## Sometimes you don't want rotation to change.   func _process(_dt):     global_rotation = 0 ```   ![missing the first line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a95b7b34-219f-43f2-8c3f-d18e728d0191)  You could argue these are both incorrect ways of writing class doc comments. If the implementation is simpler to assign the last doc comment for the class, then that's fine. But it's surprising as a user. Especially since doc comments usually precede what they annotate.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  trivially reproducible in new project.

title: GDScript 2.0: Editor type-infers closest parent with defined _init instead of the class itself
body: ### Godot version    v4.0.beta10.official [d0398f62f]    ### System information    Ubuntu 20.04, Ryzen 2700X, GTX 1070    ### Issue description    Basic example code:  ```gdscript  # Food is only there to demonstrate that it isn't a base class issue,  # but that the buck indeed stops with Fruit due to its defined _init.  class Food:  	var loadable := false    class Fruit extends Food:  	var flying := false    	func _init():  		pass    # Berry is only there to demonstrate that the buck doesn't stop with  # the parent class, but indeed is passed on to Fruit, since we don't  # have an _init defined here.  class Berry extends Fruit:  	var explody := false    # Since neither this class nor Berry have an _init defined, this will  # be inferred as Fruit, not Melon.  class Melon extends Berry:  	var extra_splashy := false  	  # Problem:  # There is an _init defined in Fruit, but not in Melon or Berry, so this  # is inferred by the editor as Fruit instead of Melon.  var melon := Melon.new()    # This works, demonstrating that godot indeed understands this as `Melon`.  print(melon.extra_splashy)  ```    At runtime, `melon` behaves as expected, but in terms of properties the editor's code completion only offers `loadable` (from grand grand parent `Food`) and `flying` (from grand parent `Fruit`, which has `_init`) from the class hierarchy, but not `explody` (from parent `Berry`) or `extra_splashy` (`Melon` - itself). Every subclass in the hierarchy past `Fruit`, which is the one with `_init`, is ignored.    Also, when using VSCode the hover-tooltip shows `Fruit` as the type of `melon`, with the same above-described completion behaviour as in Godot's builtin editor.    What I'd expect: That `melon` is type-inferred as `Melon`, not `Fruit`.    ### Steps to reproduce    The minimal reproduction project contains `bug.gd`, which has three sets of classes and corresponding examples in `_ready`. The first set demonstrates how no `_init` in the parent leads to correct type inference, the second demonstrates the problem using the Fruit example, and the third is a bit superfluous, but shows a parent and subclass who both have `_init` defined, which works as expected.    A few lines are dedicated for uncommenting for easy experimenting, with comments explaining what to do.    The project can be run in order to observe the runtime behaviour of the Fruit example. It should print: `This melon is extra splashy: false`, demonstrating how a `Melon` object which is inferred as `Fruit` indeed has the `extra_splashy` property of `Melon`, despite not showing up in the code completion drop-down.    ### Minimal reproduction project    [subclass_init_infer_bug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10304903/subclass_init_infer_bug.zip)

title: GDScripts load threading undefined behavior.
body: ### Tested versions    4.3, 3.5    ### System information    Kubuntu 22.04    ### Issue description    Just to note here to avoid confusion. The resources involved here are not manipulated after load. we're simply loading scripts for use.    **Issue 1**  This issue is about when you want to load script heavy projects. When threads are available, the loader is not using parallel threads to load independent scripts.    If you try to do it manually, if two scripts depend on another script, then you MIGHT get undefined behavior.  Loading the same resource from different threads, the issues will be different from platform to platform. Some might not reveal any problem. Some might freeze up.    One platform will be fine, while another might tell you that `GDScript` has no method called `new` !, while another one might just deadlock if you try to even load something from another thread.    I know that there is `load-threaded` that we can use in the ResourceLoader in godot 4 but that should serve mostly as a utility rather than avoiding the problem. Controlling what resource loads and where is very difficult in godot as it's done implicitly in a lot of places.    ---------------  **Issue 2**  Another issue that exists is that when you are loading a script and it references 10 other scripts that are independent of each other, those 10 scripts don't seem to be threaded. even when you use `load_threaded_request` with `use_sub_threads` set to true, it seems to ignore the fact that other scripts are dependencies.    calling `get_dependencies` also returns an empty array for a `GDScript` while it references many scripts.    ---------------  Suggestion :  - Scripts must be treated as regular resources. All referenced script paths must be cached with the editor to guide the load during runtime by knowing the dependency hierarchy. They should also be visible when calling `get_dependencies` on a `GDScript`.  - The `load` function should automatically thread for built in types that only have built in dependencies in the dependency hierarchy. Same should happen for any user defined type that it's script does not override `_init` so that loading it would have no side effects other than member variable initialization. We might want to extend this to user defined types that have some sort of script annotation set for themselves and all their dependencies. Example hirearchy :      (GDScript -> preloaded Resource with no _init -> exported variable of a type which has a special annotation).   - Possible deadlocks might happening. look out for deadlocks. I don't know how good the current threaded loading mechanism is but we need a proper scheduler.    ### Steps to reproduce    - Try to load GDScripts that both depend on another script in parallel.  - Try to load a GDScript in another thread manually.  - Make sure you test on multiple platforms including html with threads enabled. title: Deferred call of GDScript lambda from thread leads to double free or corruption when hot reloading
body: ### Godot version    v4.2.beta3.official [e8d57afae]    ### System information    Godot v4.2.beta3 - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA RTX A2000 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.2737) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11850H @ 2.50GHz (16 Threads)    ### Issue description    In Godot 4.1 I regularly use `call_deferred` to send data from a WorkerThreadPool thread back to the main thread. Usually this involves a direct function call, but occasionally I emit a deferred signal by wrapping the emit call into a lambda:  ```gdscript  (func(): test_signal.emit()).call_deferred()  ```  In Godot 4.2, this crashes the game.    Simply emitting the signal (without deferring it) does not immediately crash the game, but does not call the connected signals either.     ### Steps to reproduce    Simply create a node with the following script and attempt to run it.    ```gdscript  extends Node2D    signal test_signal    func _ready():  	test_signal.connect(test_done)  	WorkerThreadPool.add_task(T_test_func)    func T_test_func():  	print("Test processing called.")  	#test_done.call_deferred() # This works.  	#test_signal.emit() # This doesn't crash but test_done is not called.  	(func(): test_signal.emit()).call_deferred() # This crashes the game.    func test_done():  	print("Test done.")  ```    ### Minimal reproduction project    Reproduction is trivial without a dedicated project.

title: `.uid` files are not recreated if deleted by the user
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: v4.4.dev5.official.9e6098432 - Not reproducible in: 4.4.dev4 and earlier (not applicable)  ### System information  Godot v4.4.dev5 - Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (nvidia; 535.183.01) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-4570 CPU @ 3.20GHz (4 threads)  ### Issue description  If you delete the new `.uid` file for a resource (such as a .gd script), it will not be recreated and there's no way to force recreation other than deleting the .godot directory.  Bit of a weird bug because it's in part due to user error. But it's a simple mistake that gets your project into a broken state. I hit this by upgrading one of my old projects (from 4.4.dev3), a whole bunch of UID files were created and I thought "that's weird" and git clean'd them. Then I read about the design of it and realized they needed to be committed to revision control, so I tried everything I could to get them recreated, but nothing worked, other than deleting the entire .godot directory.  I gather from the design of the .uid files that this means the project is now in a broken state, as every file is expected to have a UID. I can't find any way to force the regeneration of the UID other than to delete the `.godot` directory, after which time it will create new UID files.  ### Steps to reproduce  1. Create a new project. 2. Create a new scene (just based on Node, or whatever). Save as `scene.tscn`. 3. Attach a script to that scene. Save as `scene.gd` and re-save `scene.tscn`. **Verify** that `scene.gd.uid` has automatically been created with contents: `uid://pug2wk8lb40l`. I will also note that `scene.tscn` will _not_ reference the UID - it just references `scene.gd` by filename: `[ext_resource type="Script" path="res://scene.gd" id="1_ulcgi"]`.) 4. In Godot, Reload Current Project. Re-save `scene.tscn`. **Verify** that in `scene.tscn` it _will_ refer to `scene.gd` using its UID: `[ext_resource type="Script" uid="uid://pug2wk8lb40l" path="res://scene.gd" id="1_ulcgi"]`. 5. In an external program, delete `scene.gd.uid`. 6. In Godot, Reload Current Project. **Bug**: `scene.gd.uid` will not be recreated.  So there are two seemingly related issues here: firstly, on Step 3, it's weird that the scene does not reference the UID of the script it just created. Note that I needed to add Step 4 because if you delete `scene.gd.uid` while in this state, it will actually get recreated. The .uid only doesn't get recreated after a project reload, which makes the UID show up in the .tscn file.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  [uid-recreate-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17942391/uid-recreate-issue.zip)  Project state after following the steps to reproduce above. However note that if you open this, it _will_ recreate the .uid file because the .godot directory has been removed. Try deleting the file again and note that it won't be recreated.

title: Private enum const variables show up in documentation
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee] and later Not reproducible in: v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8] and earlier. ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (nvidia; 580.159.03) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9600K CPU @ 3.70GHz (6 threads) - 30.02 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description I was working on making an asset when I made a few constants to more easily change default values when needed. Since those Constants are irrelevant for the end user, I wanted to make them private by prefixing them with an underscore, which according to the documentation will not make it appear. However I found out that they show up regardless. I was unsure if there's some weird exception to it, but when I tried to do the same with a variable, it would not show up. Which is why I made this bug report as I believe this is unintended. The only workarounds to this was to either make the const a var instead, or have the initializer be an integer value instead. Although the workaround is simple, I still believe this requires fixing. ```gdscript class_name Sample extends Node enum Rounding { FLOOR, ROUND, CEIL, } const _CONST_ENUM_ROUNDING := Rounding.ROUND # Shows up in documentation var _var_enum_rounding := Rounding.ROUND # Does not show up in documentation ``` ### Steps to reproduce - Create a script - Give it a class_name - Add an enum - Add a const variable whose default value comes from an enum. title: File picker can stall attempting to download off-device files from OneDrive
body: ### Tested versions  exhibits anomalous behavior: v4.4.dev3.official [f4af8201b] v4.4.dev6.official [1f47e4c4e]  does NOT exhibit behavior (works as expected); v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]  ### System information  Godot v4.4.dev3 - Windows 10.0.22631 - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21024.11002) - AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 6850U with Radeon Graphics (16 threads)  ### Issue description  Godot will become unresponsive and attempt to download from OneDrive if there are files in the root of the directory that are not stored on-device immediately on opening the file picker in order to open an existing project. If it's unable to download all files, it will hang. This is particularly problematic because Godot's default project directory, C:/Users/_username_/OneDrive/Documents, is synchronized with OneDrive by default.  You can work around this by creating a new, blank project by manually typing in a directory (opening the picker will cause the issue), going to the editor settings, and selecting a different default directory that's not synchronized with OneDrive.  Unsure if this extends to other kinds of symbolic links or non-local files.  I would recommend triaging by changing the default directory to C: if the problem can't be quickly resolved.  ### Steps to reproduce  - put a large file in a OneDrive synchronized folder - select "free up space" in Windows Explorer to move the file into the cloud - open the Godot file picker in said directory  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  No project needed to reproduce, bug happens before getting to the editor.

body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e], v4.7.dev2.official [778cf54da] - Not reproducible in: v4.5.stable.official [876b29033]  ### System information  Godot v4.6.1.stable - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 28 Feb 2026 14:31:21 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER (nvidia; 590.48.01) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9700K CPU @ 3.60GHz (8 threads) - 31.13 GiB memory  ### Issue description  When calling `is_valid_filename()` on a `String` or even `StringName` node property I get a crash when running a *release build on Linux*. title: Basis::set_quaternion() divides by zero when quaternion length is zero
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: 4.7.dev (commit 1aabcb9e9b)  ### Issue description  `Basis::set_quaternion()` in `core/math/basis.cpp` at line 831 divides by the quaternion's squared length without guarding against zero:  ```cpp void Basis::set_quaternion(const Quaternion &p_quaternion) {     real_t d = p_quaternion.length_squared();     real_t s = 2.0f / d;  // Division by zero if d == 0     real_t xs = p_quaternion.x * s, ys = p_quaternion.y * s, zs = p_quaternion.z * s;     ... } ```  If `p_quaternion` is a zero quaternion (w=x=y=z=0), `d` will be 0, causing `s` to become infinity (or NaN with some floating-point modes). This produces a Basis filled with NaN values that silently propagate through all subsequent matrix operations (transforms, rendering, physics).  Notably, other similar conversion functions in the codebase do guard against this. For example, `Quaternion(const Basis&)` at `quaternion.h:150` checks `Math::abs(d) > ALMOST_ONE` before dividing.  Additionally, the `Quaternion::operator Basis()` conversion path at `basis.cpp:739-741` has a similar unguarded division: ```cpp real_t s = Math::sqrt(m.rows[i][i] - m.rows[j][j] - m.rows[k][k] + 1.0f); temp[i] = s * 0.5f; s = 0.5f / s;  // Division by zero if the sqrt result is 0 ```  ### Steps to reproduce  1. Create a zero quaternion: `Quaternion(0, 0, 0, 0)` 2. Construct a Basis from it: `Basis(q)` or call `basis.set_quaternion(q)` 3. The resulting Basis contains NaN/infinity values.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  N/A — straightforward math issue visible from code analysis.

title: Wrong key mapping for XK_KP_Delete key
body: ### Tested versions  Reproducible in all Godot 4.x.y versions.  ### System information  Linux - All Godot 4.x.y versions  ### Issue description  Numeric keypad `XK_KP_Delete` key is wrongly mapped to `KP_PERIOD` instead of `KEY_DELETE` in source code file [`./godot/platform/linuxbsd/x11/key_mapping_x11.cpp` @ line 91](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/aa5b6ed13e4644633baf2a8a1384c82e91c533a1/platform/linuxbsd/x11/key_mapping_x11.cpp#L91C39-L91C39). That block of code corresponds to the key mapping of numeric keys when numlock is on, and so only `XK_KP_Decimal` is correct (and it is present [@ line 90](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/aa5b6ed13e4644633baf2a8a1384c82e91c533a1/platform/linuxbsd/x11/key_mapping_x11.cpp#L90C4-L90C4), one line above the problematic one).    `XK_KP_Delete` mapping from line 91 should be moved a few lines down (under [XK_KP_INSERT mapping @ line 107](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/aa5b6ed13e4644633baf2a8a1384c82e91c533a1/platform/linuxbsd/x11/key_mapping_x11.cpp#L107C2-L107C42)), where the numeric keypad keys are mapped for the case when numlock is off (see [comment @ line 106](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/aa5b6ed13e4644633baf2a8a1384c82e91c533a1/platform/linuxbsd/x11/key_mapping_x11.cpp#L106)) and it should look like this: `xkeysym_map[XK_KP_Delete] = Key::KEY_DELETE;`.    This bug affects all X11 based systems and it breaks the code editing workflow for programmers used to move cursor / insert / delete with the numeric keypad control keys (arrows, home / end, page up / down, insert / delete).    ### Steps to reproduce  * Ensure NumLock is off  * Write something in the code editor and try to delete using DEL key from numeric keypad  * DEL from numeric keypad doesn't work, character under cursor is not delete as expected    ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  No MRP required, the issue manifests itself all the time when using the code editor.

title: iOS export versions and product name not correctly set in generated XCode project
body: ### Godot version  4.0beta10  ### System information  macOS 13.0.1  ### Issue description  When exporting to iOS Godot generates an Xcode project you then need to run in Xcode (and often make a few last adjustments to) to test or publish your game on iOS. However, it seems that the version and product name is not configured correctly in the XCode project. If you open the target identity tab in the exported project you can see that only the bundle identifier is filled in, even though you've supplied both the versions and the game name in Godot.    ![Screenshot 2022-12-30 at 16 45 33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17763524/210088914-7081278c-4adc-4065-9126-86fbc02749df.jpg)    The reason for this is I think that these details are only filled in in the product info.plist, which one might consider correct as it's what is used in the exported final bundle. However, this does not seem like the way Xcode prefers this information to be stored, and therefor it is not displayed or used correctly in Xcode.    Instead, the preferred way to store this info for Xcode projects ([as indicated here](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information_property_list/managing_your_app_s_information_property_list?language=objc)) now seems to be to configure build settings for these properties in the project.pbxproj file (inside the .xcodeproj bundle). Namely the build settings "Bundle Display Name" (Display name), "Current Project Version" (Build) and "Marketing Version" (Version). These are then the properties used by XCode in the target identity interface etc. (And yes, this is yet another set of dictionary keys with different names for this same information, different from the interface labels and info.plist keys)    To make sure the correct info is used in the exported plist placeholders for these build settings can then be used in the plist to use the values from the build settings. title: Godot's Vulkan is non-compliant (broken) on arm32
body: ### Tested versions    4.4-master    ### System information    Godot v4.4.dev (44fa552) - Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT (RADV NAVI21) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads)    ### Issue description    RenderingDeviceDriver::id is defined as size_t:    ```cpp  class RenderingDeviceDriver : public RenderingDeviceCommons {  public:  	struct ID {  		size_t id = 0;  		_ALWAYS_INLINE_ ID() = default;  		_ALWAYS_INLINE_ ID(size_t p_id) :  				id(p_id) {}  	};  }  ```    The problem is that in ARM32 `sizeof( size_t ) == 4`.    However `VkPipeline` (and possibly others) is defined like this:    ```cpp  #define VK_DEFINE_NON_DISPATCHABLE_HANDLE(object) typedef uint64_t object;  VK_DEFINE_NON_DISPATCHABLE_HANDLE(VkPipeline)  ```    That is, VkPipeline is not a pointer. It is a uint64_t value. Yet Godot does this:    ```cpp  void RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::pipeline_free(PipelineID p_pipeline) {  	static_assert(sizeof(p_pipeline.id) == sizeof(VkPipeline), "Wrong ABI"); // This will trigger.  	vkDestroyPipeline(vk_device, (VkPipeline)p_pipeline.id, VKC::get_allocation_callbacks(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_PIPELINE));  }  ```    Basically it casts p_pipeline.id to VkPipeline; which is not legal. This will work in driver implementations that only use the first 32 bits of the variable. But it _will_ break in implementations that actually use the latter 32 bits.    This affects all Vulkan handles that are declared via `VK_DEFINE_NON_DISPATCHABLE_HANDLE`.  Vulkan objects declared via `VK_DEFINE_HANDLE`, like `VkCommandBuffer`, are meant to be actual pointers:    ```cpp  #define VK_DEFINE_HANDLE(object) typedef struct object##_T* object;  VK_DEFINE_HANDLE(VkCommandBuffer)  ```    So those are safe.    The easiest/quickest solution I see is to just make RenderingDeviceDriver::id uint64_t on all platforms. I don't know what @reduz thinks.    Another one would be to go one by one on these vulkan "non-handles" and encapsulate them in a 32 bit pointer (an extra indirection).    ### Steps to reproduce    1. Compile with `platform=android target=template_release arch=arm32`  2. Game Over.    ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)    N / A

title: iOS export: app icons are blurry when the project icon texture is loaded by an open scene
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: 4.6.2-stable  ### System information  MacBook M1 (2020), MacOS Tahoe 26.2  ### Issue description  If the texture assigned to `application/config/icon` is assigned to a TextureRect in a scene that is currently open in the editor, the iOS exporter uses a heavily compressed version of the image for the .appiconset icons. This leads to noticeable blurry images, even for the 1024 version of the icon.  ## Theory on why this happens  - Because the project icon is an imported `CompressedTexture2D`, icon export goes through `ResourceLoader::load(..., CACHE_MODE_REUSE)` and a `texture_2d_get()` readback. - `CACHE_MODE_REUSE` means that if any open scene references the icon (e.g. a TextureRect), export reuses that already-loaded, GPU-resident texture. - In this state the readback returns a degraded, downscaled-looking image, which _export_icons then upscales/resizes to every icon size producing blurry icons at all sizes.  ## Possibly relevant source code  [`platform/ios/export/export_plugin.cpp`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.6.2-stable/platform/ios/export/export_plugin.cpp) (_export_icons, line 233; project-icon branch line 286–300):  ``` icon_path = get_project_setting(p_preset, "application/config/icon"); Ref<Image> img = _load_icon_or_splash_image(icon_path, &err); ... img->resize(side_size, side_size, (Image::Interpolation)(p_preset->get("application/icon_interpolation").operator int())); img->save_png(...); ```  [`editor/export/editor_export_platform.cpp`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.6.2-stable/editor/export/editor_export_platform.cpp) (_load_icon_or_splash_image, line 95):  ``` Ref<Texture2D> texture = ResourceLoader::load(p_path, "", ResourceFormatLoader::CACHE_MODE_REUSE, r_error); if (texture.is_valid()) {     image = texture->get_image();   // CompressedTexture2D::get_image()     ... } if (image.is_null()) {              // only reached if NOT an imported resource     ImageLoader::load_image(p_path, image); } ```  [`scene/resources/compressed_texture.cpp`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.6.2-stable/scene/resources/compressed_texture.cpp) (CompressedTexture2D::get_image(), line 240):  ``` return RS::get_singleton()->texture_2d_get(texture);   // GPU/RenderingServer round-trip ```  ### Steps to reproduce  - Open the minimal project below. - Try exporting to iOS with no scenes open (you might need to supply an Apple TeamID), and look at the resulting .appiconset icons. Notice that the 1024 version looks sharp. - Now open the scene "scene_with_icon". Try exporting again, and notice that the .appiconset icons are all blurry, including the 1024 version.  A few notes - The icon.png import setting has Detect 3D set to Disabled, but this does not affect the result. title: Android frame pacing: swappy_mode values 0 and 2 are swapped in swap_chain_create
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable.mono (source inspected for the same tag) - Code path unchanged in the current `master` at the time of writing  ### System information  Godot v4.7.2.stable.mono - Android 11 - Vulkan (Mobile) - Adreno 615 - Samsung Galaxy Tab S5e (SM-T720), Snapdragon 670  ### Issue description  In `RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::swap_chain_create()` the three `swappy_mode` values are mapped to Swappy calls in an order that contradicts their own names. Values `0` and `2` are swapped.  `drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp` (4.7.2-stable):  ```cpp enum SwappyModes {     PIPELINE_FORCED_ON,     AUTO_FPS_PIPELINE_FORCED_ON,     AUTO_FPS_AUTO_PIPELINE, };  switch (swappy_mode) {     case PIPELINE_FORCED_ON:         SwappyVk_setAutoSwapInterval(true);         SwappyVk_setAutoPipelineMode(true);         break;     case AUTO_FPS_PIPELINE_FORCED_ON:         SwappyVk_setAutoSwapInterval(true);         SwappyVk_setAutoPipelineMode(false);         break;     case AUTO_FPS_AUTO_PIPELINE:         SwappyVk_setAutoSwapInterval(false);         SwappyVk_setAutoPipelineMode(false);         break; } ```  Per `thirdparty/swappy-frame-pacing/swappyVk.h`, both setters take "True means enable, false means disable":  ``` /** @brief Enables Auto-Swap-Interval feature for all instances. */ void SwappyVk_setAutoSwapInterval(bool enabled);  /** @brief Enables Auto-Pipeline-Mode feature for all instances. */ void SwappyVk_setAutoPipelineMode(bool enabled); ```  So the current mapping means:  | `swappy_mode` | Name | Auto swap interval (auto FPS) | Auto pipeline | Actually is | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0 | `pipeline_forced_on` | enabled | **enabled** | auto FPS + auto pipeline | | 1 | `auto_fps_pipeline_forced_on` | enabled | disabled | correct | | 2 | `auto_fps_auto_pipeline` | **disabled** | disabled | pipeline forced on, no auto FPS |  `0` enables auto pipeline mode although its name says the pipeline is forced on, and it enables auto FPS although its name does not mention it. `2` disables both although its name promises auto FPS and auto pipeline. Case `1` is the only one that matches its name.  The expected mapping, keeping the names, would be:  ```cpp case PIPELINE_FORCED_ON:     SwappyVk_setAutoSwapInterval(false);     SwappyVk_setAutoPipelineMode(false);     break; case AUTO_FPS_PIPELINE_FORCED_ON:     SwappyVk_setAutoSwapInterval(true);     SwappyVk_setAutoPipelineMode(false);     break; case AUTO_FPS_AUTO_PIPELINE:     SwappyVk_setAutoSwapInterval(true);     SwappyVk_setAutoPipelineMode(true);     break; ```  This matters because `swappy_mode` defaults to `2`, so projects that never touch the setting run with auto FPS *disabled* while the setting tells them the opposite, and anyone who selects `pipeline_forced_on` to avoid automatic frame-rate downshifts gets exactly the behaviour they were trying to avoid.  ### Steps to reproduce  The swap is visible in the source above without running anything. It also shows up on device

title: Imported AnimationLibrary read-only handling is incorrect after adding extra AnimationLibrary into AnimationMixer
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5 ### System information Any ### Issue description Imported Animations should not be edited, as their state reverts each time they are re-imported. The default Global (empty string) AnimationLibrary immediately after import correctly handles read-only. However, adding an AnimationLibrary to the AnimationMixer containing it breaks the read-only handling. This changes its state from "foreign" to "built-in", making it editable. Although the track has a separate imported flag that triggers the warning below, all operations are permitted in the GUI. Looking at the source code, it appears to determine this by checking whether `.import` exists in the resource path's filesystem. However, since the path changed after adding the AnimationLibrary, the determination seems to be failing. This issue has existed since version 4.1, prior to the AnimationMixer implementation, so it likely occured with the initial implementation of the AnimationLibrary. Disabling the ManageAnimationLibrary option for imported AnimationPlayers is the simplest solution, but I'm concerned about breaking compatibility. Another potential fix involves preserving the entity paths of Animations within the modified AnimationLibraryList, though I'm unsure if this is feasible. ### Steps to reproduce Add the AnimationLibrary to the imported AnimationMixer, save the .tscn file, and reopen it. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [import_animlib.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22309417/import_animlib.zip)

title: Animation tree no longer lets property settings "fall through"
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in 4.3 stable  - Not reproducible in 4.2.2 stable  ### System information  Windows 11, Godot 4.3 stable  ### Issue description  I'm working with Sprite Sheets where either the left or right direction is a mirror of the other side. I have an Animation Tree set up with an AnimationNodeStateMachine.    In the AnimationPlayer I have a dedicated animation for an Idle state, in which the property "flip h" is set to TRUE on the WEST animation, and FALSE on the EAST animation.    All the other connecting animations on either WEST or EAST side, are just copies from the opposing side that actually have sprites.    Because the animation is traveling through Idle, where the "flip h" is set, the duplicates remained playing in that direction.    This is a huge time saver and very efficient because you don't need to have dedicated animations for each direction, save for the Idle animation.    This used to work in all prior versions of Godot, except no longer in 4.3.    ![tree_bug](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/568738b6-37a7-49d5-8aed-b0885bed2162)    ### Steps to reproduce  1. Create AnimationPlayer and a Sprite(3D) with a texture of a spriteheet with an idle and walking animation.  2. Create animations Idle_EAST and Idle_WEST. Create keyframe of the frame number, and set "flip" on for the WEST animation, and off for the EAST animation. (Assuming the spritesheet has an EAST facing sprite)  3. Create animation Walk_EAST, set only the frame properties, don't touch "flip" property.  4. Create AnimationTree with State Machine  5. Add the animations Idle_EAST, Idle_WEST and Walk_EAST  6. Add again the animation Walk_EAST. This duplicate can then be renamed Walk_WEST.  7. Connect the animations so we can travel from Idle_EAST to Idle_WEST and back.  8. Connect Walk_EAST with Idle_EAST and Walk_WEST with Idle_WEST and back. Ensure that when moving from Idle to Walk, that this connection's switch mode is set to "At End", so that it does not skip Idle and therefore not set the Flip property.  9. Test the animation tree by clicking on Walk EAST and then clicking Walk WEST. Observe that even though we travel through Idle_WEST, where we flip the sprite, the flipping is ignored when we're playing Walk_WEST. Even though that animation does not override the flip setting. For a brief moment, it will flip the sprite, if the Idle animation is long enough to observe it, but then it gets reset.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  [animation_tree_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16931244/animation_tree_repro.zip)

title: Tweening modulate property doesn't behave right on 4.2
body: ### Godot version    4.2-stable_mono    ### System information    Windows 10, NVidiaRTX 2070    ### Issue description    After updating to 4.2 I've realized that all my tweens working with the property "modulate" or "self_modulate" were behaving strangely... it happens when you use loops..  for instance if you have:    ```  tween.SetLoop();  tween.TweenProperty(godotObject, "modulate", Colors.Red, 0.5f)  tween.TweenProperty(godotObject, "modulate", Colors.Blue, 0.5f);  ```    that object should change its color from red to blue and then from blue to red and then loop, right? title: CI for Linux editor builds with Mono installs .NET 6, but uses .NET 8
body: ### Tested versions    N/a    ### System information    N/a    ### Issue description    Our CI setup for Linux editor builds with Mono has a step to install .NET 6:    ```        - name: Set up .NET Sdk          uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v3          if: ${{ matrix.build-mono }}          with:            dotnet-version: '6.0.x'  ```    And it does do something. However, in the next step where we build .NET solutions, we don't actually use .NET 6. Logs suggest we're using MSBuild 17.8 which equals SDK 8.0.1xx:    ```  MSBuild version 17.8.3+195e7f5a3 for .NET  ```    See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/porting/versioning-sdk-msbuild-vs. At the same time, on our build server we do actually use .NET 6 / C# 10.    ```  Microsoft (R) Build Engine version 17.0.1+b177f8fa7 for .NET  ```    This means that builds which pass the CI do not build on the actual build server we use for official distributions. It also means we can accidentally bump our minimum supported version of .NET requirement for our internal solutions. This happened with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/82983 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/85975, which passed CI but failed on the build server.    ----    We need to either decide to actually bump the version (and update the build server), or fix up the CI and be more careful in the future.    ### Steps to reproduce    N/a    ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)    N/a

title: FreeBSD build failure: HAVE_SECURE_GETENV erroneously set for openxr dependency
body: ### Godot version  4.0.dev (040f49ed6e71a6e7f23d763c4b56095cbf319ef7)  ### System information  FreeBSD 13.1-RELEASE, GENERIC kernel, amd64  ### Issue description  When specifying the `linuxbsd` platform for scons during build, `modules/openxr/SCsub`  defines `HAVE_SECURE_GETENV` for the `openxr` third-party dependency. This define  implies the existence of the function `secure_getenv` – which FreeBSD doesn't have.    That in turn leads to the build currently failing on FreeBSD when it encounters [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/040f49ed6e71a6e7f23d763c4b56095cbf319ef7/thirdparty/openxr/src/common/platform_utils.hpp#L53):  ```cpp  #ifdef HAVE_SECURE_GETENV      return secure_getenv(name);  ```    I can confirm that commenting out the define of `HAVE_SECURE_GETENV` in  [modules/openxr/SCsub](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/040f49ed6e71a6e7f23d763c4b56095cbf319ef7/modules/openxr/SCsub#L37) fixes said build failure *on FreeBSD*, but am not too  sure how to fix this without finally introducing BSD as its own platform.    I also can't speak on whether the other BSDs provide `secure_getenv`,  but a cursory check for corresponding man pages on [man.openbsd.org](https://man.openbsd.org/secure_getenv)  and [man.netbsd.org](https://man.netbsd.org/secure_getenv) yields no results.  ### Steps to reproduce  * Run `scons platform=linuxbsd` on FreeBSD  ### Minimal reproduction project  _No response_

title: HarfBuzz on 4.7 needs explicit hb-raster linkage
body: ### Tested versions  4.7-stable  ### System information  NixOS  ### Issue description  When building Godot 4.7 with system HarfBuzz, the build requires explicit linkage to `hb-raster` symbols, but the build configuration only requests `harfbuzz` and `harfbuzz-icu` via pkg-config. In packaging environments with strict dependency/linking behavior, this leads to link failures unless `-lharfbuzz-raster` is added manually.  In `nixpkgs`, this currently requires a workaround: ```export NIX_LDFLAGS="$NIX_LDFLAGS -lharfbuzz-raster"```  The expectation is that Godot build scripts should request/link the required HarfBuzz raster component directly when raster APIs are used.  Related NixOS PR: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/533148  ### Steps to reproduce  1. Build Godot 4.7 with: `builtin_harfbuzz=false` and LTO enabled (or in strict packaging environments) 2. Use system HarfBuzz 13+ with raster support built-in  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  N/A

title: Layered Textures imported with BPTC has image layers of differing signedness
body: ### Tested versions  current master  ### System information  Godot v4.6.1.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.4.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Max (Apple9) - Apple M4 Max (16 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory  ### Issue description  When importing an image as a layered texture with BPTC compression, the resulting image layers can have differing signedness. This is due to how we currently compress the images: `Image::detect_signed()` reports that one image layer is signed, so that gets compressed as BPTC signed, but subsequent image layers may be reported as unsigned (e.g. if it happens to have any color values that would trigger the detection).   As a result, the layered texture is unable to be loaded, as the rendering server refuses to load images of differing formats.  ### Steps to reproduce  Download the MRP Open in editor Observe that the texture is incorrectly displayed as all white in the resource preview and the logs indicate that it failed to load due to mismatched image formats  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  https://github.com/nikitalita/mrp-repo/releases/download/v1.0.0/bptc-mrp.zip

body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: 4.5-rc1  ### System information  Godot v4.5.rc1 - Fedora Linux 42 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon Graphics (radeonsi, renoir, ACO, DRM 3.63, 6.15.10-200.fc42.x86_64) - AMD Ryzen 9 4900HS with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 38.58 GiB memory  ### Issue description  Godot does not import normal maps specified in `.mtl` files like this:  ``` map_Bump -bm 1.000000 Textures/T_Plaster_Normal.png ```  Apparently such an MTL file was created by Blender 4.0.2 (it comes from a Quaternius asset pack), so I think this format should be supported.  We can see in the source code why it does not work:  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2dd26a027a99633231184616d4dd287bbdd1c0a3/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_obj.cpp#L177-L184  Firstly it does not consider `map_Bump` (which may be nonstandard, but evidently is used).  Secondly, it does not consider the possibility of texture options such as `-bm 1.000000` appearing before/after the path.  In this context a quote from [the Wikipedia article on the OBJ format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavefront_.obj_file#Vendor-specific_alterations) is relevant:  > According to the spec, options are supposed to precede the texture filename. > However, at least one vendor generates files with options at the end.   ### Steps to reproduce  1. Open the MRP 2. Notice the missing normals (the bricks should stick out from the wall).  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  [godot_obj_wall_bump_2025-09-09_11-31-47.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22230975/godot_obj_wall_bump_2025-09-09_11-31-47.zip)

title: PS4/Dual Shock 4 controller analogue input causes actions to ignore other connected controllers' analogue input events
body: ### Tested versions    Reproducible in v4.2.1.stable.official [b09f793f5]    ### System information  Dual Shock 4 (PS4 controller) + other controllers (I used xbox, PS5, etc). Copied info: Godot v4.2.1.stable - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.3623) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-4690 CPU @ 3.50GHz (4 Threads)  ### Issue description  With multiple controllers connected, if one is a PS4/DS4 controller, other controllers' analogue inputs for an action shared by the PS4/DS4 will often be ignored when getting the action strength.    Getting the action strength seems to behave correctly exactly when a controller changes its axis value, but the action strength quickly zeroes again, presumably related to how 'flickery' the raw DS4 analogue input is.    To be clear:  - digital (non-analogue) inputs are not interrupted  - playing with a controller is fine if the DS4 is not connected  - playing with a DS4 is fine even if other controllers are connected  - using Input.get_joy_axis() behaves as expected even when the DS4 is interfering with action strength    I assume this is related to a previous bug where the PS4 controller would make keyboard input actions cut out despite being stronger. It may have existed then too and just not been noticed.    sorry if this report isn't the best, I'm not used to doing this! I'll help more if I can.  ### Steps to reproduce  Attach my code to a label, have a "Left" action in the InputMap with an event listening for analogue stick left.  You'll need the PS4/DS4 controller and at least one other kind of controller, both connected.    You'll notice the "Input Action" will frequently go to 0 when using a non-DS4 controller while the DS4 is connected, and works fine if the DS4 is unplugged. The DS4 itself seems to work fine.  As you can see from the get_joy_axis() values, all controllers are reporting their values correctly, the issue is with the action strength.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  ```  extends Label    func _process(delta):  	var actionName = "Left"  	# cuts to 0 sometimes if a DS4 is connected:  	text = "Input Action:" + str(Input.get_action_strength(actionName))     	# inputs from specific gamepads still report correctly  	var events:Array[InputEvent] = InputMap.action_get_events(actionName)  	var analogueInput:InputEventJoypadMotion  	for e in events:  		if e is InputEventJoypadMotion:  			analogueInput = e    	for j in Input.get_connected_joypads():  		text += "\n" + Input.get_joy_name(j) + str(Input.get_joy_axis(j, analogueInput.axis))  ```

title: Fail to export Android release when any of (but not all) debug keystore environment variables are set
body: ### Tested versions  Reproducible in: `4.5-beta5` `4.4.1 stable`, `4.3 stable` Untestable at: `4.0.0 stable` (The scenario cannot be tested, because there is already an error in the editor in the export popup `missing configuration for debug keystore`.)  ### System information  Arch Linux SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 02 Aug 2025 01:20:06 +0000 - Wayland - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 570 Series (RADV POLARIS10) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-7600K CPU @ 3.80GHz (4 Threads)  ### Issue description  When attempting to export a Godot project to Android in release mode, the export process erroneously fails if any debug keystore-related environment variables (`GODOT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_DEBUG_USER`, `GODOT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_DEBUG_PASSWORD`, `GODOT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_DEBUG_PATH`) are set.  The specific error message received is: `ERROR: Cannot export project with preset "android" due to configuration errors: Either Debug Keystore, Debug User AND Debug Password settings must be configured OR none of them.`  [export.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21740103/export.log)  This behavior is undesirable because, during a release mode export, the presence or absence of debug keystore configurations or associated environment variables should be entirely irrelevant to the export. The release build should exclusively rely on the specified release keystore settings. The current implementation incorrectly validates debug keystore information even when it is not applicable to the requested export mode, thus preventing successful release builds under these circumstances.  ### Steps to reproduce  1. Execute the export command, ensuring `godot` is in your system's `PATH`: ``` env GODOT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_DEBUG_USER=androiddebugkey godot --headless --verbose --export-release android "./output.apk" ``` Note: The env command temporarily sets the `GODOT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_DEBUG_USER` environment variable for the duration of this command, simulating a scenario where debug keystore variables are present in the environment.  Actual result: Error due to missing information relevant to `debug` keystore. Expected result: Error due to missing information relevant to `release` keystore.  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  The ZIP is empty project created with `4.3 stable` version containing export template for Android. [android-release-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21740131/android-release-test.zip)

body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in: master (61598c5c88), 4.3, possibly all the way back to 3.3.  The code of interest was introduced in commit 221f5da85 on 2021-08-15.  I apologize for not including an MRP, but this is a bug in a method exported via the gdextension API and I do not believe the bug can be reproduced with GDScript, C#, or godot-cpp because none of them ever call the method in question. I am working on SwiftGodot (Swift language bindings for Godot).   ### System information  macOS 14.7.1 - Godot 4.3 or master (61598c5c88)  ### Issue description  In `variant_op.h` lives the class `OperatorEvaluatorModNZ` which implements the `%` operator, and at [line 301](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L301-L323) begins the specialization for the class for `Vector2i % Vector2i`:  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L301-L323  At [line 312](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L312) it uses the overloaded C++ operator `%`  operator on behalf of GDScript:  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L312  At [line 317](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L317) it again uses the overloaded C++ `%` for gdextensions calling through the `Variant` API:  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L317  But at [line 320](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L320), it **incorrectly** uses the overloaded C++ operator `/` for gdextensions calling through the pointer API:  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f952bfe9985ad8f507cc29b2c7601bbba18b8039/core/variant/variant_op.h#L320  Line 320 needs to be changed to also use operator `%`.  ### Steps to reproduce  Write new language bindings that use the engine to compute `Vector2i % Vector2i`.  In my case, I am writing test cases that compare what the engine returns and what my native Swift code computes, to verify that my Swift code matches the engine behavior. Imagine my surprise when the engine gave the wrong answer!  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  I don't think it's feasible to include an MRP. Reproducing the problem requires creating new language bindings, because none of GDScript, C#, and godot-cpp rely on this exported engine method.

title: C# Not exported in debug builds
body: ### Tested versions  - Reproducible in 4.6.dev4.mono, 4.6.dev3.mono, 4.6.dev2.mono - Not reproducible in 4.5.1.mono  ### System information  Godot v4.6.dev4.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7688) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-14400F (16 threads) - 31.83 GiB memory  ### Issue description  When exporting any C# project in a debug build. It doesn't seem to include .cs files in the .pck file. This causes debug builds to fail. ``` ERROR: Cannot open file 'res://Main.cs'.    at: (modules/mono/utils/string_utils.cpp:152) ERROR: Failed to read file: 'res://Main.cs'.    at: (modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2807) ERROR: Cannot load C# script file 'res://Main.cs'.    at: (modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2887) ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://Main.cs.    at: (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:343) ERROR: Can't load dependency: 'res://Main.cs'.    at: (core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp:459) ERROR: Error when trying to parse Variant.    at: (core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp:503) ERROR: Error when trying to parse Variant.    at: (core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp:490) ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://.godot/exported/133200997/export-3070c538c03ee49b7677ff960a3f5195-main.scn.    at: (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:343) ERROR: Failed loading scene: res://main.tscn.    at: (main/main.cpp:4595) ```  ### Steps to reproduce  1. Create a new C# project 2. Write any C# code and attach it to a node 3. Export the project with debug  ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)  [csharp-test_2025-11-18_20-08-20.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23606349/csharp-test_2025-11-18_20-08-20.zip)
